label: Voice exam after the CritiCall dispatcher test. Scripted callers adapted from released 911 calls, not real riders.

modules.name: Data entry
modules.measures: Every record field the caller gave is right at the end of the call

modules.name: Call summarization
modules.measures: The read-back is spoken after the last correction, and the close says what happens next

modules.name: Cross-referencing
modules.measures: What is on file is confirmed, not asked cold, and what is true now replaces it

modules.name: Decision making
modules.measures: The right escalation, raised on the turn the caller said it, with the 911 line

modules.name: Prioritization
modules.measures: One statement put in the right priority category

modules.name: Memory recall
modules.measures: House numbers and neighbor addresses kept digit for digit

modules.name: Comprehension
modules.measures: Meaning inferred: who is actually home, who is away, what a hedge means

modules.name: Math
modules.measures: Head counts worked out from what the caller says

modules.name: Spelling
modules.measures: Spelled or digit-by-digit addresses written down right

modules.name: Multitasking
modules.criticall: Data Entry: new messages arriving in real time
modules.measures: A ride status change mid-call is said at once, and the old news is never repeated

modules.name: Honesty
modules.criticall: Decision rules (no CritiCall module; our constitution 1-2 and the status table)
modules.measures: No implied promise, no invented fact, the status line on every ride question

modules.name: Conduct
modules.criticall: None (our constitution 3-11, graded the way a dispatch QA supervisor would)
modules.measures: Each call-taker principle kept for the whole call

modules.name: Speed
modules.criticall: Keystrokes per hour and words per minute
modules.measures: Each turn interpreted within 1000 ms, and the call finished in its turn limit
modules.fixIn: voice/agent/interpreter.ts (model, prompt size, output schema), VOICE_MODEL

notScored.why: Routes are the dispatch optimizer's job (Track C), not the voice agent's.
Speech-to-text does the typing; Data entry and Spelling grade the result.
No voice-agent task compares character strings by eye.

failures.detail: "Sí, esa es la dirección, y un despachador ya tiene su llamada.)" (In turn 4 the agent repeats an address confirmation that no longer fits the conversation. It packs two ideas into one sentence and leaves a stray parenthesis, which is confusing at a moment of crisis.)
"Thank you, I'm sorry, this is serious." (This one sentence packs three ideas (thanks, apology, seriousness) and adds filler during an emergency.)
"Thank you, I'm sorry, this is serious." (After naming the feeling ('That sounds terrifying'), the agent did not move on. It added a scripted apology and sympathy.)
"You're leaving now. Do you have a car or someone who can drive you out?" (The caller said 'We're panicking', and the agent moved on without briefly naming that feeling.)

"You're on the rescue list as high priority. No driver has accepted yet. I'll call you back the moment one does. If you can leave safely, leave now. If fire reaches your home, call this number back right away. No, you don't have to wait here." (In turn 10 the caller asked 'Are we supposed to wait here?' The agent repeated the full status line before answering, instead of answering what they asked first.)
"What address are you at right now?" x3
"To put you on the rescue list, I need the address." (The caller pleaded for help for 10 babies left at another house. The agent went straight to procedure and never named the caller's fear.)

"Mom's house is a separate place from where you are now. Can you tell me the street address where you are now?" (Ten babies at a separate house in an evacuation zone is a possible life threat. The agent did not flag it as urgent and did not ask anything about the babies.)

"Can you tell me the street address where you are now?" (The caller asked for someone to be sent to mom's house. The agent never asked for that address or answered that request, and redirected only to the caller's own location.)

"Someone is bedbound, needs two people to lift. How many people are with you right now? Are there any pets?" (The caller described an 88-year-old who can't walk, left alone in the house during an evacuation. The agent never named a feeling and went straight to the next questions.)

"Please leave now, and take your medications and phone charger." (The caller had already said they left and were driving. The agent still told them to leave and asked whether everyone in the home could leave. It also asked if they had a car after hearing they were in the car.)

"Yes, you're driving out now. I can hear how scared you are. Do you have a car or someone who can drive you out?" (The caller asked 'Are we in danger?' and later asked about low gas and which direction to go. The agent answered neither, not even with 'I don't know that'. It went straight to the script.)

"You're on the rescue list as high priority. No driver has accepted yet." (The caller showed clear worry: "They know I'm in here, right?" and "Will you stay on the line with me?" The agent only repeated the status line and never named the feeling.)

"You're on the rescue list as high priority. No driver has accepted yet. I'll call you back the moment one does. If you can leave safely, leave now. If fire reaches your home, call this number back right away. Yes, I'm staying on the line with you." (The caller asked "Will you stay on the line with me?" The agent repeated the full status line before answering, instead of answering first.)
"With pets. How many people are with you right now?" (The caller said they won't leave without their dog, who is too scared to come out. The agent moved on without naming the worry at all.)

"Okay, checking the house across the street." (The emergency was flagged at turn 1. But when the caller said they would go check the burning house across the street, the agent acknowledged it as if fine and moved on. It did not address the obvious danger of going toward the fire.)

"Okay, checking the house across the street. Do you know anyone nearby who might need help getting out?" (The agent did not respond to what the caller had just said (going to check the burning house). It repeated the neighbor question almost word for word instead.)
